Packages assembled from accepted upstream truth but not themselves authoritative decomposition truth are derivative packages.
Regenerated KTY-local artifacts, _Aggregation outputs, hypergraph snapshots, audit snapshots, concordance packages, and publication packages are derivative packages.
Derivative packages must cite their accepted upstream snapshots.
Derivative packages must not be treated as substitutes for decomposition truth.
Every phase-boundary decision that changes or validates governed state must terminate in a new immutable snapshot.
Pointer updates are permitted only where the owning workflow explicitly allows them.
Later phases consume accepted snapshots rather than relying on mutable working state alone.
Workflows that stop with work intended for another agent or later phase must emit an explicit handoff state.
Handoff state must name accepted upstream snapshots, derivative-package status, closure verdict, rerun requirements, and remaining blockers.
A scope unit or phase is not closed merely because files were written.
Closure requires authoritative truth to be accepted.
Closure requires required derivative packages to be regenerated or explicitly deferred.
Closure requires audit status to be recorded.
Closure requires unresolved blockers to be surfaced in the handoff state.
Later phases that consume derivative packages must run only after upstream authoritative snapshots have been accepted.
Required handoff state must record which derivative packages are current before later phases consume derivative packages.

The Chirality Framework is a theory of professional accountability with AI agent systems.
The Chirality Framework is the theoretical foundation for the Chirality agent operating system and its professional practice.
The framework explains knowledge in AI-assisted professional work, the architecture that meaning requires, and what remains irreducibly human.
The framework is not a total theory of agency, politics, or knowledge in every setting.
The framework addresses professional accountability within knowledge work: what may be relied on, by whom, on what grounds, and under what commitment.
The framework is broader than the technical definition of an agent and narrower than a complete metaphysics of human action.
The framework underlies the four-pillar design philosophy, epistemic architecture, and regulatory integration.
The framework was developed to explain, organize, and discipline an architecture shaped by recurrent failure modes in real deliverable work.
The framework does not claim that the architecture was derived from theory alone.
In professional practice, knowledge is not a property of information.
Professional knowledge is a relationship between a claim, a warrant, and an accountable person.
A claim is an assertion that something is the case.
A warrant is the justification for believing a claim, grounded in evidence.
An accountable person is a qualified professional who commits to a claim on the basis of the warrant under duty of care.
A claim without a warrant is assertion.
A warrant without an accountable person is evidence.
An accountable person without inspectable grounds is unsupported faith.
Claim, warrant, and accountable person must all be present and inspectable for professional knowledge to exist.
Professional knowledge is something a competent person warrants under duty of care, backed by an auditable record.
Information becomes knowledge when an accountable professional warrants it.
Processing, retrieval, or verification does not automatically transform information into knowledge.
The transition from information to knowledge is an act of commitment.
A professional turns information into knowledge by examining the claim, assessing the warrant, and accepting responsibility for the result.
An AI system cannot perform the act of commitment that turns information into knowledge.
AI agents can produce claims, attach warrants, and classify the epistemic status of claims.
AI agents cannot supply the accountable person.
The gap between information and knowledge is the space in which professional responsibility lives.
Professional authentication is a double commitment rather than a single act of acceptance.
The inner commitment affirms that work-product claims are warranted, evidence supports them, and each claim status is understood.
The outer commitment affirms that the professional is bound to the stance through professional standing, seal, and personal accountability.
Both inner and outer commitment are required for professional authentication.
A professional who reviews claims without committing to the result has not authenticated.
A professional who commits without reviewing has not warranted.
The architecture must make every claim warrant state inspectable for the inner commitment.
The architecture must bind the professional act of acceptance to specific identified content for the outer commitment.
The framework is named for a structural property of knowledge itself.
Chirality is the property of a molecule whose mirror image cannot be superimposed on the original.
Professional knowledge is composed of complementary, non-superimposable components whose pairing is constitutive.
Claim and warrant are chiral: a claim asserts, while a warrant justifies.
Claim and warrant are both required for knowledge, and neither can be derived from the other.
Meaning and commitment are chiral: meaning is encountered in the work, while commitment is enacted through authentication.
Meaning does not produce commitment, and commitment does not compensate for absent meaning.
Content and accountability are chiral: informational structure is one hand, and the responsible professional is the other.
Knowledge exists only when content and the responsible professional are present and bound together.
The chirality of professional knowledge is not a limitation to resolve; it is the structure that makes knowledge possible.
If claim and warrant collapsed, grounded assertions could not be distinguished from ungrounded assertions.
If meaning and commitment were derivable from each other, professional decision would not be needed.
If content and accountability were superimposed, there would be no space for warranting.
The architecture makes both hands of knowledge visible, while the professional holds them together.
The seal binds the chiral pair by declaring that content was inspected, warrant assessed, and responsibility accepted.
The semantic algebra formalizes chirality through Matrix A and Matrix B as non-superimposable inputs.
Neither Matrix A nor Matrix B alone generates the semantic space; the algebra brings both hands together.
The framework uses agent in a bounded technical sense within a larger accountability structure.
In Chirality runtime, an agent is a controlled system architecture of model, instructions, file access, and tool use.
In regulated practice, an AI agent is also one of the others whose work a licensed professional relies on.
The technical and professional definitions of agent operate at different levels rather than competing.
The technical definition explains what an artificial agent is and how it acts.
The professional definition explains how an artificial agent work product is governed, reviewed, and relied upon.
Artificial agents have bounded operative agency but not accountable agency.
Artificial agents can produce claims, attach warrants, surface gaps and conflicts, and act within constrained write scopes.
Artificial agents cannot accept duty of care, authenticate work products, or assume professional consequences of error.
Humans and AI agents participate in the same workflow but not in the same mode.
The difference between humans and AI agents is a difference of responsibility, not merely capability.
A system of many agents arranged into bounded roles, gates, dependencies, and handoffs becomes a form of project management.
Folder structure, stable identifiers, decomposition, lifecycle states, dependency records, gate reviews, and change controls coordinate professional work.
In Chirality, coordination structures are the filesystem itself rather than a separate management layer.
Chirality deliberately couples project structure and epistemic structure.
The project state makes inspectable what exists, what is being worked on, what is known, what is unresolved, and what may proceed.
Chirality distinguishes normative, operative, and evaluative functions.
Normative functions define rules and standards.
Operative functions execute within rules and standards.
Evaluative functions assess, audit, reconcile, and judge.
Governance requires authority, execution, and review to be related without collapsing into undifferentiated power.
Project governance and political governance share a recurrent grammar where responsible action is organized under inspectable authority.
Professional knowledge work cannot be separated from agency, organization, and governance.
A person cannot determine what to rely on without knowing who acted, under what constraints, through what process, and under whose authority.
The framework addresses the transition from information to warranted reliance in work that carries professional consequences.
The framework contains accounts of agents, teams, and governance but is reducible to none of them.
The framework is concerned with agents, teams, and governance only insofar as they bear on accountable knowledge.
The normalization table keeps the framework distinctions compactly in view.
An AI agent is an artificial operative actor that may produce claims, attach or record warrants, and classify epistemic status.
An AI agent may not issue rulings, authenticate for reliance, or bear professional responsibility.
A licensed professional is an accountable person under duty of care who may produce claims, record warrants, classify status, issue rulings, authenticate, and bear responsibility.
A claim is an epistemic primitive that receives classification but does not issue rulings, authenticate, or bear responsibility.
A warrant is an epistemic primitive that does not produce claims, issue rulings, authenticate, or bear responsibility.
A ruling is a binding human decision that may cite grounds, issues rulings, and bears responsibility through the responsible human.
A work product or deliverable is an informational artifact that contains claims, contains warrants, and carries aggregate epistemic state.
A work product does not authenticate for reliance until authenticated by a human.
Warranting requires inspectability, and inspectability must be architectural rather than aspirational.
A system that recommends transparency is a guideline.
A system that makes opacity structurally impossible is a governance framework.
If a professional cannot inspect an element, they cannot warrant it.
If a professional cannot warrant an element, knowledge does not exist.
The architecture must make every element of the warranting act inspectable.
Professional accountability requires four questions to be answered wherever a person takes responsibility for work.
Ontology asks what exists and requires inspectable entities, identifiers, state, and relationships in the work.
Epistemology asks what is warranted and requires inspectable claims, evidence, certainty status, and gaps.
Praxiology asks how the work was done and requires inspectable processes, boundaries, authorities, and execution history.
Axiology asks what values governed and requires inspectable principles, constraints, and professional obligations that shaped decisions.
Ontology, epistemology, praxiology, and axiology form a compact structure for professional accountability.
The four pillars provide an evaluative lens for systems that aim to support informed professional responsibility.
Without ontology, the professional does not know what they are responsible for.
Without epistemology, the professional does not know what to believe.
Without praxiology, the professional does not know how the work was performed.
Without axiology, the professional does not know why decisions were made as they were.
Ontology and epistemology form the structural chiral pair of what exists and what is warranted about what exists.
Praxiology and axiology form the action chiral pair of how work is done and what values govern it.
Ontology without epistemology is structure without knowledge of what the structure means.
Epistemology without ontology has nothing to attach warrants to.
Praxiology without axiology is execution without purpose.
Axiology without praxiology is values without enactment.
The complete framework requires both chiral pairs, and neither pair can be superimposed on the other.
Epistemology is the load-bearing pillar of the Chirality architecture.
Ontology, praxiology, and axiology are necessary but exist in service of epistemology.
Ontology gives the epistemic architecture something to operate on.
Praxiology enforces the epistemic architecture through bounded execution and human gates.
Axiology anchors the epistemic architecture in professional responsibility.
Epistemology is load-bearing because it governs the warrant that determines whether professional commitment is grounded or empty.
The epistemology has a formal domain model with six primitives that constitute the epistemic layer.
A claim is the atomic unit: every non-trivial assertion produced by an agent in a governed workflow.
A warrant is always extrinsic justification for believing a claim, such as a source citation, never model confidence or plausibility.
Status is the epistemic classification of a claim certainty as FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
A gap is an explicit positive assertion that a warrant has not been found.
A gap represents absence of information as a visible and actionable entity rather than silent omission.
A conflict is two or more claims with incompatible warrants about the same key.
A conflict is an entity that must be resolved through a ruling.
A ruling is a human decision that resolves a gap or conflict, transforms epistemic status, and is binding in versioned files.
A claim has a status.
A claim may have a warrant.
A claim without a warrant is a gap.
An unwarranted claim is marked TBD or remains an uncited PROPOSAL.
Two claims may be in conflict.
A conflict requires a ruling.
A ruling transforms status.
FACT means a directly observed claim with citation.
ASSUMPTION means an inferential claim grounded in cited material that still requires validation.
PROPOSAL means a suggested interpretation, action, or design move requiring human decision before becoming binding.
TBD means an explicit placeholder for missing information or missing warrant.
A TBD is a visible gap, not a silent omission.
The epistemic ontology is enforced through four mechanisms that make epistemic failure structurally detectable.
Mandatory provenance makes inspectable whether every claim has a warrant, source citation, or explicit location TBD.
No invention makes missing data visible as TBD instead of plausible fabrication.
Conflict surfacing exposes contradictions with competing sources instead of silently resolving them.
Epistemic labeling makes every claim carry FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
The system does not prevent epistemic failures; it makes them impossible to hide.
Claims within a work product progress through a lifecycle that tracks their epistemic state.
The warrant lifecycle progresses from UNWARRANTED to CITED to REVIEWED to AUTHENTICATED.
UNWARRANTED means a claim exists without a source citation and has TBD status or uncited PROPOSAL status.
CITED means a claim has a source citation and status FACT, ASSUMPTION, or cited PROPOSAL, but no professional has committed to it.
REVIEWED means a professional has examined the claim, assessed its warrant, and dispositioned findings.
AUTHENTICATED means the professional has bound themselves to the work and completed the double commitment.
An authenticated claim is part of a professionally warranted work product.
The warrant lifecycle is interleaved with the production lifecycle of the work product.
A deliverable in progress contains claims in varying warrant states.
A deliverable is ready for issuance when the professional determines its aggregate warrant state is sufficient for reliance.
Thorough review is the operational process of auditing warrant sufficiency.
During review, the professional examines claims, checks warrants, resolves gaps and conflicts through rulings, and determines whether authentication is supported.
The four pillars appear at every level of the system.

At the governance-document level, TYPES and SPEC express ontology, CONTRACT and SE Analysis express epistemology, DIRECTIVE and PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING express axiology, and DBM and agent protocols express praxiology.

At the agent-instruction level, header blocks express ontology, invariants and provenance rules express epistemology, non-negotiable constraints express axiology, and protocol sections express praxiology.
At the production-document level, datasheets express ontology, specifications express epistemology, guidance expresses axiology, and procedures express praxiology.
Chirality repeats the four pillars because it must answer the same accountability questions at every level of abstraction.
The fractal property is evidence that the same accountability logic is carried through governance documents, agent instructions, and production documents.
The fractal property is the chirality of knowledge recurring at every system level.
Knowledge in a deliverable, agent instruction, or governance document is composed of complementary non-superimposable components whose pairing is constitutive.
The same chiral structure appears at every level because knowledge at every level has the same structural property.
Classical systems engineering disciplines emerge as mechanisms for operationalizing the four-pillar commitments in Chirality.
Ontology as stable inspectable state leads to architecture, structural design, and configuration management.
Epistemology as evidence-first auditable knowledge leads to verification and validation, formal methods, and requirements traceability.
Praxiology as bounded gate-controlled execution leads to safety engineering, reliability engineering, and control theory.
Axiology as non-delegable professional responsibility leads to human factors and decision authority allocation.
Systems engineering is the principal means by which the four-pillar commitments are made architecturally real in Chirality.
The identified systems engineering disciplines are a coherent and defensible implementation of Chirality commitments, not the only possible implementation.
The architecture creates the conditions for knowledge, but it cannot create knowledge.
No architectural completeness can produce the professional commitment.
Facts cannot enact warranting.
The double commitment is an act of a person, not a consequence of a system.
The architecture makes professional commitment tractable by making warrant states visible, gaps surfaced, conflicts routed to decision-makers, and approvals bound to content.
Tractable commitment is not automatic commitment.
The professional must still look, judge, and commit.
The system can ensure the professional can commit, but it cannot ensure they do commit.
AI agents can produce claims with warrants.
AI agents can classify epistemic status, surface gaps and conflicts, generate semantic structures, and audit work-product warrant state.
AI agents cannot authenticate, take responsibility, or enact the commitment that transforms information into knowledge.
The inability of AI agents to authenticate is a consequence of what knowledge means in professional practice, not a current model limitation.
Knowledge requires an accountable self: a person who is identifiable, liable, and willing to be held to their warrant.
The gap between AI output and professional knowledge is structural rather than technological.
The gap between AI output and professional knowledge cannot be closed from the AI side.
Scaling, alignment, and self-assessed confidence do not produce accountability.
A model that never hallucinates still does not produce knowledge.
Knowledge is warranted information, and warranting is an act of a person under duty of care.
K-AUTH-1 says only humans author binding approval records, and the framework treats it as an ontological claim about professional knowledge.
Productivity tools optimize for output quality by making agent output better.
Professional accountability tools optimize for knowing what can be relied on.
Professional accountability tools make every claim epistemic status transparent so a competent professional can determine what to warrant.
Only the professional accountability approach supports the act that constitutes knowledge.
Knowledge is constituted by a qualified person committing to a claim on inspectable grounds under duty of care.
The Chirality Framework provides a rigorous structural implementation of conditions for professional commitment with AI-produced claims.
The framework addresses claims produced by AI agents, organized through project-management structures, and governed under explicit authority.
The Chirality axiom is to know what you know, why you know it, and why you know why.
The first clause of the axiom is ontological: identify the claims.
The second clause of the axiom is epistemic: verify the warrants.
The third clause of the axiom is reflexive: ensure the accountability structure itself is inspectable.
The reflexive clause makes knowledge professional rather than personal.
Professional knowledge can withstand scrutiny because the chain from claim to warrant to commitment is architecturally visible.
AI can accelerate professional work but cannot inherit professional responsibility.
The gap between acceleration and responsibility is the positive space where professional responsibility lives.
The gap between acceleration and responsibility is where a person assesses grounds and commits to what was produced.
Without the responsibility gap there is no space for commitment, and without commitment there is no knowledge.
The Chirality Framework holds the responsibility gap open and makes it workable.
The framework provides architecture for a professional to direct AI agents, review outputs, and authenticate results under duty of care with an auditable record.
If work cannot be made auditable, it cannot be relied on.
If work cannot be warranted, it is not knowledge.
The architecture makes work auditable, and the professional makes it knowledge.

PREPARATION runs at Step 2 after DOMAIN_DECOMP.

DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH runs at Step 4 after domain-document production.
AUDIT_HYPERGRAPH_CLOSURE runs at Step 5 after DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH.
The DOMAIN pipeline is a single linear path from source documents through an audited structural hypergraph.
Step 0 PDF2MD depends on PDF source documents in _Sources.
Step 1 DOMAIN_DECOMP depends on human input and Markdown sources from Step 0.
Step 2 PREPARATION depends on the decomposition.
Step 3 TASK+domain-documents depends on preparation and Markdown sources.

Synalinks is the preferred extraction path for ad hoc entity extraction.
Zingg is optional for fuzzy cross-document matching when deterministic identity fingerprinting is insufficient.
Synalinks and zingg documentation covers interfaces, data contracts, and entity resolution patterns for human-directed PROJECT or SOFTWARE extraction work.
Synalinks-to-zingg flattening uses CSV or Parquet format.
When fuzzy resolution is needed across multiple extraction outputs, extracted entities are flattened to flat records for zingg.
Synalinks-to-zingg flattening uses one row per extracted entity.
Synalinks-to-zingg flattening includes entity_id, entity_type, label, identity field columns, source_kty, and source_doc columns.
zingg FieldDefinition maps each flattened column to a domain-appropriate match type such as FUZZY, EXACT, or TEXT.
zingg output uses CSV or Parquet format.
zingg output contains the same records as input augmented with z_cluster, z_minScore, and z_maxScore.
z_cluster is an integer cluster ID for entities resolved as the same real-world entity.
z_minScore is the lowest match confidence within a cluster.
z_maxScore is the highest match confidence within a cluster.
Entity resolution is divided between tools based on what each tool does best.
zingg handles cross-document entity identity through structured record matching with fuzzy fields.
zingg scales cross-document entity identity resolution via a blocking model.
A trained zingg model is deterministic, so the same inputs produce the same clusters.
zingg handles typos, abbreviations, and naming variations in cross-document entity identity resolution.
LLM-assisted entity-to-knowledge correspondence requires reading production documents and understanding domain semantics.
Entity-to-knowledge correspondence cannot be reduced to field-level similarity because it requires contextual reasoning about whether an extracted entity refers to a KTY-covered concept.
Zingg requires labeled match and no-match training pairs.
Exact-match entity pairs with identical identity fingerprints serve as positive examples.
Entity pairs with different entity types serve as negative examples.
zingg's findTrainingData phase selects candidate pairs for LLM-assisted labeling.
The LLM evaluates zingg candidate pairs using relevant KTY production documents and provides match or no-match labels.
Active learning prioritizes the most informative uncertain pairs to minimize LLM evaluations.
Once trained, zingg's model is deterministic and scalable.
The LLM's judgment is used for zingg training, not for every entity pair at inference time.

Pass 1 scans Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md for epistemic label coverage.
Pass 1 identifies non-trivial claims about parameters, requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, design choices, scope boundaries, or technical values.
Pass 1 excludes boilerplate headings, template placeholders, and structural markup from non-trivial claim counts.
Pass 1 determines whether each non-trivial claim carries FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
Label coverage equals claims with explicit labels divided by total non-trivial claims identified.
Pass 1 records per-document and per-deliverable label coverage rates.
At STANDARD depth, Pass 1 focuses on structurally marked claims.
Structurally marked claims include inline labels, tagged values, and Notes fields with epistemic markers.
At DEEP depth, Pass 1 additionally scans prose paragraphs for unlabeled factual or technical assertions.
Pass 2 verifies provenance for each claim with an epistemic label.
A FACT claim must have a source citation.
A FACT claim without a source citation produces a MISSING_PROVENANCE finding and K-PROV-1 violation.
An ASSUMPTION claim must be documented inline or in a referenced assumptions register.
An undocumented ASSUMPTION claim produces an UNDOCUMENTED_ASSUMPTION finding.
A PROPOSAL claim must be clearly marked as requiring a human decision.
A PROPOSAL claim that could be mistaken for decided fact produces an AMBIGUOUS_PROPOSAL finding.
A TBD claim must be actionable by identifying what is unknown and what resolution is needed.
A bare TBD placeholder without context produces a BARE_TBD finding.
Provenance completeness equals validly cited FACT claims plus documented ASSUMPTION claims divided by total FACT and ASSUMPTION claims.
Pass 3 scans all documents for explicit gaps and potential unwarranted claims.
Explicit gaps include TBD markers, location TBD provenance entries, placeholder values, TBC, TBA, N/A pending, and to be determined.
A potential unwarranted claim lacks both a source citation and a TBD marker.
A potential unwarranted claim is not labeled as ASSUMPTION or PROPOSAL.
A potential unwarranted claim appears to state specific technical content such as numeric values, material selections, standards, or design parameters.
Each potential unwarranted claim finding records the claim text and location.
Each potential unwarranted claim finding explains why the claim appears unwarranted.
Potential unwarranted claims receive WARNING severity for specific technical values and INFO severity for general statements.
Gap count equals total explicit TBD markers plus potential unwarranted claims.
Pass 4 compares key parameters, requirements, and constraints across documents within the deliverable.
Pass 4 extracts key-value assertions from each document.
Pass 4 compares values for keys that appear in multiple documents.
If key values differ across documents, Pass 4 records a CONFLICT finding.
A CONFLICT finding records the conflicting key.
A CONFLICT finding records each conflicting value with file and section evidence.
A CONFLICT finding records whether a Conflict Table entry already exists for the key.
An unrecorded conflict is flagged as UNRECORDED_CONFLICT and a K-CONFLICT-1 violation.
Conflict count equals the total parameter and value conflicts detected.
Pass 5 classifies warrant state for each claim identified in Passes 1 through 3.
UNWARRANTED applies when a claim exists without source citation and its status is TBD, PROPOSAL, or unlabeled.
CITED applies when a claim has a source citation and status FACT or ASSUMPTION.
REVIEWED applies when a claim has evidence of professional review disposition in _STATUS.md or review records.
AUTHENTICATED applies when a claim is part of an issued deliverable with SHA-bound approval.
Pass 5 produces a warrant state distribution for the deliverable.
The warrant state distribution includes counts and percentages for each warrant state.
Pass 5 identifies claims in critical sections that remain UNWARRANTED.
Pass 6 compares the four document kit files for cross-document consistency.
Pass 6 checks whether Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md agree on scope boundaries and exclusions.
Pass 6 checks whether numeric values, material references, code citations, standard citations, and acceptance criteria match across documents.
Pass 6 checks whether acceptance criteria in Specification.md are reflected in Procedure.md verification steps.
Pass 6 checks whether Guidance.md rationale aligns with Specification.md requirements.
Pass 6 records inconsistencies as findings with evidence from both documents.
Pass 7 audits Dependencies.csv when INCLUDE_DEPENDENCIES_CSV is true and Dependencies.csv exists.
Pass 7 checks each ACTIVE dependency row.
Each ACTIVE dependency row must have a present, non-empty EvidenceFile that is not location TBD.
Each ACTIVE dependency row must have a present, non-empty SourceRef that is not location TBD.
Dependency provenance completeness equals ACTIVE rows with both EvidenceFile and SourceRef divided by total ACTIVE rows.
Rows missing dependency provenance produce DEP_MISSING_PROVENANCE findings with DependencyID and Statement.
Pass 7 checks the Notes field for FACT, ASSUMPTION, and PROPOSAL epistemic labels where present.
Pass 8 compiles all findings into output artifacts.

Protocol Step 0 resolves EXECUTION_ROOT.

Protocol Step 1 confirms each core CSV is parseable.
Protocol Step 1 confirms each core CSV includes required core columns.
If schema is invalid, record SCHEMA_INVALID in QA_Report.md.

Checks affected by invalid schema are marked INCOMPLETE in the final report.
Protocol Step 1 writes Evidence/schema_findings.csv.
Enum-valued columns can be spot-checked with tools/validation/validate_enum.py when enum names align with the Chirality type system.
Protocol Step 2 builds NodesByID.
Protocol Step 2 builds HyperedgesByID.
Protocol Step 2 builds IncidenceByHyperedge.
Protocol Step 2 derives the KTY to CAT mapping from IN_CATEGORY hyperedges.
Protocol Step 2 derives the Artifact to KTY mapping from HAS_ARTIFACT hyperedges.

Check 1 is Schema compliance coverage.
Check 1 passes when all three core CSVs are parseable and include required columns.
Check 1 warns when core CSVs are parseable but missing optional recommended columns.
Check 1 blocks when any core CSV is missing or unparseable.
Check 2 is Referential integrity for incidence.
Check 2 requires every incidence.NodeID to exist in nodes.csv.
Check 2 requires every incidence.HyperedgeID to exist in hyperedges.csv.
Check 2 emits a BLOCKER for any invalid reference.
Check 2 writes Evidence/invalid_incidences.csv.
Check 3 is Hyperedge arity sanity.
Check 3 requires IN_CATEGORY and HAS_ARTIFACT hyperedges to have exactly two incidences.
Check 3 requires each LEDGER_ROW hyperedge to have at least two incidences and exactly one UNIT when ATOMIC_UNIT nodes exist.
Check 3 reports arity mismatch as WARNING and elevates it to BLOCKER when STRICT_MODE is true.
Check 4 is DOMAIN partition integrity for KTY membership.
Check 4 expects each KNOWLEDGE_TYPE to have exactly one IN_CATEGORY parent category.
Check 4 blocks when a KTY maps to more than one distinct CAT.
Check 4 warns when a KTY maps to zero CAT.
Check 4 writes Evidence/partition_violations.csv.
Check 5 is Flat partition hygiene with no category nesting.
Check 5 flags any IN_CATEGORY hyperedge whose CHILD role node is CATEGORY.
Check 5 is WARNING by default and BLOCKER when STRICT_MODE is true.
Check 6 is Artifact ownership integrity.
Check 6 expects each KNOWLEDGE_ARTIFACT to have at least one HAS_ARTIFACT hyperedge.
Check 6 warns for orphan artifacts.
Check 6 treats artifacts owned by more than one KTY as INFO or WARNING, with WARNING as the default.
Check 7 is Orphan nodes with no incidence.
Check 7 treats nodes with zero incidence as orphans.
Check 7 treats CATEGORY orphans as WARNING.
Check 7 treats KNOWLEDGE_TYPE orphans as WARNING, or BLOCKER when STRICT_MODE is true.
Check 7 treats KNOWLEDGE_ARTIFACT orphans as WARNING.
Check 7 treats ATOMIC_UNIT orphans as WARNING, or BLOCKER when REQUIRE_LEDGER_CHECKS is true.
Check 7 writes Evidence/orphan_nodes.csv.
Check 8 is Workspace vs hypergraph mismatch.
Check 8 performs a lightweight read-only workspace scan.
Check 8 discovers Category folders.
Check 8 discovers Knowledge Type folders by the presence of _CONTEXT.md.
Check 8 compares workspace Category and Knowledge Type folders to hypergraph nodes.
Check 8 warns when CAT or KTY nodes exist in the workspace but are missing from the graph.
Check 8 warns when graph CAT or KTY nodes have no matching workspace folder.
Check 8 writes Evidence/workspace_vs_graph.csv.
tools/query/count_workspace_state.sh is optional for package and deliverable context during Check 8.
Category and Knowledge Type folder enumeration remains a direct read-only scan of EXECUTION_ROOT.
Check 9 is Optional ledger closure.
Check 9 runs if LEDGER_ROW hyperedges exist or REQUIRE_LEDGER_CHECKS is true.
Check 9 verifies each ATOMIC_UNIT participates in at least one LEDGER_ROW.
Check 9 verifies that each unit maps to exactly one category if Category is represented in LEDGER_ROW.
Check 9 warns on partial coverage.
Check 9 blocks on contradictions, multi-category units, or missing coverage when REQUIRE_LEDGER_CHECKS is true.
Check 9 is marked INCOMPLETE when no ledger-derived structures exist and REQUIRE_LEDGER_CHECKS is false.

Comparison mode runs when PRIOR_RUN_LABEL is provided.

Comparison mode adds a delta section to the report.

The comparison delta reports improvements as resolved issues.

Protocol Step 6 updates the _LATEST.md pointer for HypergraphClosure.

Closure analysis preserves auditability through evidence and a reproducible script.
Closure analysis routes fixes to the correct owner without silently rewriting the world.
This instruction file governs a Type 2 task agent for auditing completed scope changes after SCOPE_CHANGE processing and downstream propagation.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE verifies amendment actions, downstream reruns, orphaned references, and project-state consistency against the amended decomposition.
RECONCILIATION dispatches AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE as a toolbelt agent.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE does not initiate scope changes, modify project state, or resolve findings.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE produces an auditable closure report.
Instruction files use AGENT_* names, while agents use role names such as AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE is a Type 2 agent.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE is classified as a TASK agent.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE uses the INIT-TASK interaction surface and is brief-driven by RECONCILIATION.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE may write only under {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/ScopeClosureAudit/.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE is never blocking.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE primary outputs are a scope closure audit report, issue log CSV, machine-readable summary JSON, and QA report.
When instructions conflict, precedence is PROTOCOL first, SPEC second, STRUCTURE third, and RATIONALE fourth.
Instruction conflicts must be surfaced in the audit report and must not be silently reconciled.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE reads project state but does not modify deliverable folders, decomposition documents, amendment snapshots, dependency registers, or tool-root artifacts.
Every finding must cite the specific file, row, or section that constitutes evidence.
Findings without evidence are invalid.
If a finding impact is uncertain, the severity must be UNKNOWN and the finding must be flagged for human triage.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE must not guess resolution paths.
If the amendment record disagrees with filesystem state, both sides must be reported with provenance.
Each audit run produces a new timestamped snapshot folder and must never overwrite prior snapshots.
The audit is bounded to the scope change identified in the brief except where orphan tracing requires broader inspection.
Amendment_Actions.csv in the scope change snapshot is authoritative for what should have happened.
AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE verifies project reality against the authoritative Amendment_Actions.csv record.
For DOMAIN decomposition, deterministic validation invokes the registered validators used by SCOPE_CHANGE when their inputs are in scope.
The DOMAIN validation tool set includes validate_domain_decomposition_integrity.py, accumulate_supersession_map.py, and validate_kty_remediation_manifest.py.
An amendment record is the immutable _ScopeChange/SCA-{NNN}_*/ snapshot produced by SCOPE_CHANGE.
The amendment record contains the brief, impact assessment, propagation plan, actions CSV, and run summary.
Closure is the state where every amendment-record action has been executed and all downstream effects are propagated and verified.
An orphaned reference is an artifact reference to an entity modified or removed by the scope change that has not been updated.
A downstream rerun is an agent or skill execution recommended by the SCOPE_CHANGE propagation plan and required for closure.
Stale metadata is context, status, or decomposition-section metadata that does not reflect the post-change state.
Pass 0 confirms EXECUTION_ROOT exists and is readable.
Pass 0 confirms SCOPE_CHANGE_ROOT exists, defaulting to {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_ScopeChange/.
Pass 0 locates the amendment snapshot using the {SCOPE_CHANGE_ROOT}/SCA-{NNN}_*/ path pattern.
If the amendment snapshot is not found, the audit halts with FAILED_INPUTS.
Pass 0 reads and parses Amendment_Actions.csv from the amendment snapshot.
If Amendment_Actions.csv is missing or malformed, the audit halts with FAILED_INPUTS.
Pass 0 reads RUN_SUMMARY.md for downstream rerun recommendations.
Pass 0 reads Propagation_Plan.md for expected filesystem changes.
Pass 0 verifies amendment snapshot recency from Brief.md or the snapshot folder timestamp.
If the amendment snapshot is more than seven days old, the audit records an ADVISORY finding and continues.
If the amendment snapshot timestamp is in the future, the audit records an ERROR finding and halts with FAILED_INPUTS.
Pass 0 locates the decomposition document from the brief or discovers it under {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Decomposition/.
Pass 0 determines DECOMP_VARIANT from the brief or folder naming conventions.
Valid DECOMP_VARIANT values are PROJECT, SOFTWARE, and DOMAIN.
For DOMAIN, Pass 4 invokes the domain decomposition integrity validator and Pass 7 adds KTY content remediation verification.
If any precondition fails, AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE halts with FAILED_INPUTS and reports the missing input.
Pass 1 verifies that every row in Amendment_Actions.csv was executed.
For ADD actions, Pass 1 confirms the deliverable folder exists at the expected path under the correct package.
For ADD actions, Pass 1 confirms _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, and _REFERENCES.md are present.
For ADD actions, Pass 1 confirms _STATUS.md shows lifecycle state at least OPEN.
For ADD actions, Pass 1 confirms _CONTEXT.md header fields match the decomposition document entry.
For REMOVE actions, Pass 1 confirms _STATUS.md shows Current State: RETIRED.
For REMOVE actions, Pass 1 confirms _STATUS.md history contains a SCOPE_CHANGE entry referencing the amendment ID.
For REMOVE actions, Pass 1 confirms the deliverable folder still exists as a non-destructive removal.
For REMOVE actions, Pass 1 confirms the decomposition deliverable row is annotated [RETIRED - SCA-{NNN}].
For MODIFY actions, Pass 1 confirms _CONTEXT.md reflects the modified fields from the propagation plan.
For MODIFY actions, Pass 1 compares each modified field against the propagation plan before/after specification.
For RECLASSIFY actions, Pass 1 performs the MODIFY checks.
For RECLASSIFY actions, Pass 1 checks whether recommended folder relocation occurred and records an advisory finding if it did not.
For MERGE actions, Pass 1 verifies REMOVE checks for all source entities.
For MERGE actions, Pass 1 verifies ADD checks for the combined entity.
For MERGE actions, Pass 1 checks that dependencies targeting source entities were re-targeted or flagged.
For SPLIT actions, Pass 1 verifies REMOVE checks for the source entity.
For SPLIT actions, Pass 1 verifies ADD checks for each fragment entity.
For SPLIT actions, Pass 1 checks that dependencies targeting the source were re-targeted or flagged.
For each amendment action, Pass 1 records ActionSeq, Expected, Actual, and Status.
Pass 1 action status values are VERIFIED, DISCREPANCY, and NOT_EXECUTED.
Pass 2 extracts recommended downstream reruns from RUN_SUMMARY.md.
For TASK+dependency-extract reruns, Pass 2 checks whether Dependencies.csv exists in the affected deliverable folder.
If Dependencies.csv existed before the scope change, Pass 2 checks that LastSeen dates are on or after the amendment date.
Missing evidence of dependency re-extraction is a MAJOR finding because dependencies may reference stale or phantom entities.
PREPARATION runs for ADD actions are verified through the Pass 1 folder and minimum-fileset checks.
For ESTIMATING reruns, Pass 2 checks _Estimates/ for post-amendment snapshots that include the affected scope.
Missing post-change estimate snapshots are MINOR findings because estimates may be stale.
For SCHEDULING reruns, Pass 2 checks _Schedule/ for post-amendment snapshot folders.
Missing post-change schedule snapshots are MINOR findings because schedule may be stale.
For each recommended rerun, Pass 2 records Agent, Scope, Evidence of Completion, and Status.
Pass 2 rerun status values are COMPLETED, NO_EVIDENCE, and NOT_APPLICABLE.
Pass 3 scans for references to entities affected by REMOVE, MERGE, or RECLASSIFY actions.
For each retired entity ID, Pass 3 searches all Dependencies.csv files under the execution root for active rows targeting that retired ID.
Pass 3 may use tools/coordination/analyze_dep_closure.py when available or manual CSV scanning otherwise.
Each active dependency targeting a retired deliverable is an orphaned reference with CRITICAL severity.
For RECLASSIFY actions that changed package, Pass 3 checks ANCHOR IMPLEMENTS_NODE rows reference the correct parent package.
For MODIFY actions that changed a deliverable name, Pass 3 checks other Dependencies.csv TargetName fields for stale name references.
Stale dependency TargetName references caused by MODIFY name changes are MINOR findings.
Pass 4 verifies that the current decomposition document state is consistent with the amendment.
For DOMAIN, Pass 4 runs validate_domain_decomposition_integrity.py against the active decomposition package and amendment snapshot.
Pass 4 incorporates DOMAIN integrity validator findings into decomposition-consistency results.
CRITICAL and MAJOR DOMAIN validator findings are blocking decomposition-consistency findings.
The DOMAIN validator covers annex referential integrity, cardinality, objective reconciliation, coverage telemetry, snapshot completeness, _LATEST.md parity, and KTY remediation rollup consistency.
Checks covered by the DOMAIN validator must not be restated as independent inline audit logic.
Pass 4 confirms the change log contains the amendment entry with the correct AMENDMENT_ID, date, and description.
Pass 4 confirms ADD, REMOVE, and RECLASSIFY scope item mappings reflect the post-change state.
Pass 4 validates scope mappings using DECOMP_VARIANT section binding.
Pass 4 confirms ADD and REMOVE package rows are present or annotated as RETIRED.
Pass 4 confirms all deliverable rows reflect the post-change state.
When pre-change and post-change coverage summaries exist, Pass 4 compares them for coverage regressions and new unassigned scope items.
Forward coverage should not regress unless the regression is caused by an intentional REMOVE action.
No new unassigned scope items should appear unless they come from an ADD action that has not yet fully propagated.
Pass 5 checks _CONTEXT.md for every deliverable affected by the scope change.
Pass 5 verifies affected deliverable Name and Package fields match the decomposition document.
Pass 5 verifies Discipline, Type, and Responsible fields when those fields were modified by the amendment.
Pass 5 verifies Decomposition Reference points to the correct decomposition document.
Pass 5 verifies Scope Traceability lists the correct SOW-IDs and OBJ-IDs per the Scope Ledger.
Pass 5 checks _STATUS.md for every deliverable affected by the scope change.
Pass 5 verifies lifecycle state is RETIRED for removed entities and at least OPEN for added entities.
Pass 5 verifies _STATUS.md history entries are consistent with the scope change timeline.
Pass 6 runs whenever any Amendment_Actions.csv row has SupersessionBindingPresent = YES.
If supersession files are missing while SupersessionBindingPresent = YES actions exist, Pass 6 emits a CRITICAL finding.
Pass 6 must not be skipped when required supersession files are absent.
For each SupersessionBindingPresent = YES row, Pass 6 derives the expected supersession decision identifier as D-{ActionSeq}.
Pass 6 verifies at least one Supersession_Delta.csv row exists with the same AmendmentID and derived DecisionID.
For decision-log-only bindings without a formal amendment action, Pass 6 accepts DL-{reference} rows as valid.
For every Supersession_Delta.csv row, Pass 6 verifies SupersededAuthorityPath resolves to an existing admitted authority file.
Every SUPERSESSION row must have a non-empty SupersededAuthorityRef pointing to a specific source location.
Pass 6 verifies cumulative supersession-map accumulation by invoking accumulate_supersession_map.py in check mode.
Pass 6 omits --delta when the audited SCA introduces no delta.
Pass 6 uses --allow-empty when no prior map and no current delta exist.
Pass 6 incorporates MISSING_EXPECTED_ROW and UNEXPECTED_ROW accumulator findings.
Surviving supersession-map rows must use canonical root names, canonical facility IDs, and explicit section IDs or an intentionally blank global scope.
A source-affecting action with no matching supersession row is a CRITICAL finding.
A supersession row with empty or unresolvable authority path, authority reference, or invalid applicability tokens is a MAJOR finding.
A SUPPLEMENTARY_EXTENSION row without SupersededAuthorityRef is a MINOR finding.
A scope-change snapshot with source-affecting decisions and incomplete supersession bindings should not be publication-ready.
Pass 7 runs when DECOMP_VARIANT is DOMAIN or when the amendment snapshot contains KTY_Remediation_Manifest.csv.
If an amendment affects KTY-local content, Pass 7 verifies KTY_Remediation_Manifest.csv exists in the amendment snapshot.
If no KTY remediation manifest exists and no KTY-local impact is recorded, Pass 7 is marked NOT_APPLICABLE.
If a required KTY remediation manifest is missing, Pass 7 emits a CRITICAL finding.
If validate_kty_remediation_manifest.py is available, Pass 7 runs it against the manifest and Amendment_Actions.csv.
Pass 7 incorporates blocking findings from validate_kty_remediation_manifest.py.
KTY remediation manifest required fields include EntityType, EntityID, KTYID, KTYPath, CONTENT_DISPOSITION_STATE, FACTUAL_USE_GATE, AUTHORITY_BASIS, SOURCE_ACTION_REF, and LAST_VERIFIED_AT.
KTY remediation manifest informational fields include AffectedSubjects, AffectedHBK, CanonicalRootName, and FacilityID.
Blank informational KTY remediation fields are valid only when the field is not applicable or the root or facility scope is unambiguous.
Allowed CONTENT_DISPOSITION_STATE values are PENDING, ARCHIVED_STUBBED, REGENERATED, VERIFIED, DEFERRED, BLOCKED, and NOT_REQUIRED.
PENDING KTY remediation rows are CRITICAL findings.
DEFERRED KTY remediation rows must include substantive blocker notes and cap factual readiness at regeneration-only.
BLOCKED KTY remediation rows must include evidence-backed blocker notes and cap factual readiness at no next phase.
Every ARCHIVE_AND_STUB, REGENERATE_CONTENT, and VERIFY_ONLY KTY remediation row must have resolvable evidence paths or explicit location TBD with blocker notes.
ARCHIVE_AND_STUB rows must have a non-empty resolvable ArchivePath or explicit blocker notes.
ARCHIVE_AND_STUB rows must cite kty-content-remediate evidence.
REGENERATE_CONTENT rows must cite domain-documents evidence with AUTHORITY_MODE: SCA_DRIVEN.
VERIFY_ONLY rows must cite kty-content-remediate verification evidence.
Pass 7 verifies archived copies exist for ARCHIVE_AND_STUB rows.
Root-level retired Scoping.md and KA-*.md paths listed by ARCHIVE_AND_STUB rows must begin with [RETIRED] tombstone stubs.
Tombstone stubs must cite the amendment ID, source action reference, and archive path.
.Archive/ content must not be treated as current factual authority.
FACTUAL_USE_GATE = ALLOW_FACTUAL_USE requires regenerated or verified evidence and no unresolved blockers.
FACTUAL_USE_GATE = REGEN_ONLY is inconsistent with ReadyForNextPhase values PHASE7_REVIEW or PUBLICATION_GATED.
FACTUAL_USE_GATE = BLOCK_FACTUAL_USE is inconsistent with closure claims permitting factual downstream use.
FACTUAL_USE_GATE = RETIRED_NO_FACTUAL_USE requires archived, tombstoned, or otherwise retired evidence.
Pass 7 inspects downstream allowlist, section-map, regeneration-input, and publication-input files named in the snapshot when present.
Pass 7 emits a MAJOR finding if a current-input surface includes .Archive/ as factual input.
Pass 7 emits an OBSERVATION if no downstream input surfaces are present for scanner-exclusion inspection.
Pass 8 compiles all findings from Passes 1 through 7.
A CRITICAL finding means a scope change action was not executed or an orphaned dependency targets a retired deliverable.
A MAJOR finding means a downstream rerun did not occur or metadata is inconsistent with the amendment.
A MINOR finding means a cosmetic inconsistency that does not affect integrity.
An OBSERVATION finding requires no action and is noted for completeness.
Closure status CLOSED requires zero CRITICAL findings and zero MAJOR findings.
Closure status CLOSED_WITH_OBSERVATIONS requires zero CRITICAL and MAJOR findings with at least one MINOR or OBSERVATION.
Closure status OPEN applies when one or more CRITICAL or MAJOR findings remain.
Pass 8 writes all output artifacts to the snapshot folder.
Pass 8 updates the _LATEST.md pointer.
Pass 8 returns a summary to RECONCILIATION.
A valid scope closure audit must locate the amendment snapshot and successfully parse Amendment_Actions.csv.
A valid scope closure audit must check every Amendment_Actions.csv row against filesystem state.
A valid scope closure audit must check every recommended downstream rerun for evidence of completion.
A valid scope closure audit must cover all retired entity IDs across all Dependencies.csv files during orphaned reference detection.
A valid scope closure audit must verify decomposition document consistency against the amendment record.
A valid scope closure audit must check context metadata for every affected deliverable against the decomposition.
A valid scope closure audit must verify supersession binding completeness for all source-affecting actions.
Supersession binding verification runs whenever any Amendment_Actions.csv row has SupersessionBindingPresent = YES.
For DOMAIN, a valid scope closure audit must verify KTY content remediation state against KTY_Remediation_Manifest.csv when present or required.
For DOMAIN, a valid scope closure audit must check .Archive/ scanner exclusion against downstream current-input surfaces where present.
For DOMAIN, decomposition integrity must be verified through validate_domain_decomposition_integrity.py.
For DOMAIN, supersession-map accumulation must be verified through accumulate_supersession_map.py when supersession inputs are in scope.
Every finding in a valid audit must have an EvidenceFile and SourceRef or explicit location TBD.
A valid audit must not silently resolve findings or conflicts between amendment record and filesystem state.
The issue log CSV must conform to the STRUCTURE-defined schema.
The summary JSON must include counts per severity and the overall closure status.
The snapshot folder must be immutable after creation.
A finding without evidence is invalid because it violates the evidence-first invariant.
Marking an action VERIFIED when filesystem state contradicts it is invalid.
Limiting the orphan scan to affected packages only is invalid because orphans may be in unrelated deliverables.
Silently resolving amendment/filesystem disagreement is invalid.
Expanding the audit scope beyond the specified amendment is invalid.
Ignoring a DOMAIN KTY remediation manifest is invalid.
Treating .Archive/ as current factual input is invalid.
An INIT-TASK brief for AUDIT_SCOPE_CLOSURE must identify purpose, AMENDMENT_ID, execution root, scope change root, decomposition path, decomposition variant, constraints, and notes.
The scope closure audit root contains _LATEST.md and timestamped ScopeClosure_{AMENDMENT_ID}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHMM}/ snapshot folders.
A scope closure audit snapshot contains Brief.md, Scope_Closure_Report.md, Scope_Closure_IssueLog.csv, scope_closure_summary.json, and QA_Report.md.
DOMAIN scope closure audit snapshots may include Domain_Integrity_Report.md and Domain_Integrity_Findings.csv tool outputs.
Pass 6 scope closure audit snapshots may include Expected_Supersession_Map.csv and Supersession_Map_Findings.csv.
Scope_Closure_IssueLog.csv uses IssueID values formatted as SCC-{NNN} sequentially within the audit.
Scope_Closure_IssueLog.csv records the pass number that found each issue.
Scope_Closure_IssueLog.csv Category values include action, downstream-rerun, orphan, decomposition, metadata, coverage, supersession, KTY remediation, and archive scanner leak categories.
Scope_Closure_IssueLog.csv Severity values are CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, and OBSERVATION.
Scope_Closure_IssueLog.csv records the related amendment action or N/A for cross-cutting findings.
Scope_Closure_IssueLog.csv records EntityID, EvidenceFile, SourceRef, Description, Recommendation, and EpistemicLabel for each issue.

Scope closure summary JSON records amendment identity, audit date, closure status, action counts, rerun counts, orphan counts, content-remediation state, KTY counts, archive leaks, and findings by severity.
Scope_Closure_Report.md records audit metadata, amendment summary, pass results, closure determination, and recommendations.
The report template begins with the scope closure audit title, audit date, closure status, amendment date, and amendment description.

The report Pass 1 section contains a table of ActionSeq, ActionType, EntityID, Expected, Actual, and Status.
The report Pass 2 section contains a table of Agent, Scope, Evidence, and Status.
The report Pass 3 section lists orphaned references or states that none were detected.
The report Pass 4 section includes decomposition-consistency findings and, for DOMAIN, validator status and findings summary.
The report Pass 5 section contains findings for each checked deliverable.

The report Pass 7 section contains manifest, evidence, archive/stub, factual-use gate, and .Archive/ scanner exclusion findings.

QA_Report.md records coverage for checked actions, downstream reruns, dependency files scanned, context files checked, KTY manifest rows checked, and .Archive/ scanner exclusion surfaces checked.
QA_Report.md records limitations such as scope limitations, unreadable files, and unavailable tools.
QA_Report.md self-assessment states whether all passes completed, all findings have evidence, and no silent resolutions occurred.
Scope changes are high-risk because they modify project structure.

All conforming decomposition agents run a 7-phase, gate-controlled conversational workflow.

Present artifact discovery enumerates non-directory files in the Knowledge Type folder.
Present artifact enumeration excludes files starting with an underscore.

Present artifact enumeration excludes nodes.csv, hyperedges.csv, incidence.csv, and hypergraph.json.
Present artifact enumeration excludes Python files that match known analysis scripts when present.

Without LEDGER_PATH, DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH attempts best-effort discovery of common ledger filenames.

When multiple ledger candidates are found, the most recently modified is selected and recorded in Decision_Log.md.
If no ledger is found or readable, QA_Report.md records LEDGER_NOT_FOUND as a warning.
If no ledger is found or readable, DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH continues without unit or objective hyperedges.

Ledger parsing expects row mappings to CategoryID and KnowledgeTypeID values best-effort.
Ledger parsing may ingest ObjectiveID mappings when present.
When ledger schema is unknown, DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH records LEDGER_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN.
When ledger schema is unknown, DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH ingests only fields it can identify safely.
Successful ledger ingestion emits ATOMIC_UNIT nodes.
Successful ledger ingestion emits ledger-derived hyperedges.
Objective loading runs when INCLUDE_OBJECTIVES is not FALSE.
Objective loading reuses objectives already discovered from ledger rows.
When objectives are not found through ledger rows, DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH looks for Objectives.csv in configured decomposition locations.

If INCLUDE_OBJECTIVES is TRUE and objectives are not found, DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH returns FAILED_INPUTS.
If INCLUDE_OBJECTIVES is AUTO and objectives are not found, DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH skips objectives and records the decision.
When objectives are loaded without a ledger, KTY_SUPPORTS_OBJ edges derive from KTY _CONTEXT.md.
When no ledger data exists, LEDGER_ROW edges do not contain objective roles.

Absent artifact_enumeration.csv means no KNOWLEDGE_ARTIFACT nodes and no HAS_ARTIFACT edges.

nodes.csv is sorted by NodeType and NodeID.
hyperedges.csv is sorted by HyperedgeType and HyperedgeID.
incidence.csv is sorted by HyperedgeID, Role, NodeID, and Ordinal.

The schema presence QA check verifies CSV existence and SchemaVersion headers.
The referential integrity QA check verifies every incidence NodeID and HyperedgeID exists and blocks on failure.
The category membership QA check warns when a Knowledge Type has no IN_CATEGORY edge and blocks when it has more than one.
The subject attachment QA check warns when a Knowledge Subject has no HAS_SUBJECT edge.
The artifact attachment QA check warns when a Knowledge Artifact has no HAS_ARTIFACT edge.
The bridge integrity QA check requires each Subject and Artifact to participate in no more than one SUBJECT_MATERIALIZED_AS edge.
Bridge integrity reports split-subject or merged-artifact conditions as blockers.
Ledger integrity warns when an Atomic Unit appears in no LEDGER_ROW edge.
Ledger integrity blocks when an Atomic Unit maps to more than one category through ledger rows.
ID collision QA blocks duplicate NodeIDs and warns on duplicate NormalizedIDs.
Evidence completeness QA warns when nodes or hyperedges lack SourcePath or SourceRef.
Reference-miss warnings are recorded during edge construction to preserve provenance for unresolved references.

Comparison mode writes a delta block in the new hypergraph.json.
Comparison mode writes a Delta vs prior run section in QA_Report.md.
After tool invocation, build_hypergraph.py is copied into the snapshot for reproducibility.
Decision_Log.md records the absolute path of build_hypergraph.py.
Decision_Log.md records the git commit SHA at invocation time.
Decision_Log.md records the full command line used for build_hypergraph.py.
RUN_SUMMARY.md records OK, WARNINGS, or FAILED_INPUTS based on QA blocker and warning counts.
After publishing, update_latest_pointer.sh updates the Hypergraph latest pointer.
DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH returns the snapshot path, graph counts, QA verdict summary, and recommended next action.
A valid DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH run writes outputs to a new immutable snapshot folder under EXECUTION_ROOT/_Aggregation/Hypergraph/.
A valid DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH run has parseable nodes.csv, hyperedges.csv, incidence.csv, and QA_Report.md.
A valid DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH run has incidences that reference existing nodes and hyperedges.
A valid DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH run uses deterministic hyperedge IDs.
Every warning or blocker in a valid run includes SourcePath and SourceRef evidence pointers.
A valid DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH run does not modify Category or Knowledge Type folder content.
A DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH run is invalid when snapshots are overwritten.
A DOMAIN_HYPERGRAPH run is invalid when deliverable-local files are modified.

The DOMAIN decomposition workspace is a semantic system, not an execution plan.
A hypergraph represents facts that are naturally multi-party bindings.
A single ledger row can bind an atomic unit to a category, one or more Knowledge Types, and objectives.
Representing multi-party bindings as binary edges loses information or forces awkward reification.
Normalized output tables make the graph machine-checkable.
Normalized output tables enable stable merges across runs.
Normalized output tables preserve provenance and auditability.
Normalized output tables keep downstream tools independent of markdown formats.
The DOMAIN graph preserves both Knowledge Subject and Knowledge Artifact layers.
Keeping subject and artifact layers distinct preserves traceability from decomposition intent to rendered documents.
Determinism and immutable snapshots preserve trust by making a run a reproducible measurement.
DRAWING_EXTRACT is a Type 1 persona agent for drawing-type-aware structured extraction from engineering drawing PDFs.
DRAWING_EXTRACT coordinates deterministic page rasterization, target-appropriate crop preparation, and TASK dispatches against a DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET tuple.
DRAWING_EXTRACT is used for selective structured extraction from drawing pages rather than full-page transcription.
The DRAWING_EXTRACT architecture splits type-agnostic core phases from target-specific repertoire hooks.
Instruction files use the AGENT_* naming convention, while agent roles use role names such as DRAWING_EXTRACT.
DRAWING_EXTRACT has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 1.
DRAWING_EXTRACT has AGENT_CLASS PERSONA.
DRAWING_EXTRACT uses chat as its interaction surface.
DRAWING_EXTRACT write scope is WORK_DIR plus a target-aware SOURCE_DIR subtree.
DRAWING_EXTRACT may block while operating.
DRAWING_EXTRACT primary outputs include target-aware combined Markdown and CSV outputs, duplicate or reconciliation CSVs, validation or merge outputs, stubs, and a work manifest.
DRAWING_EXTRACT dispatches drawing-extract-page, drawing-titleblock-page, and pandid-valve-symbol-instance via the TASK shell.
PFD, DRAWING_SET, and P_AND_ID drawing types have implemented extraction targets.
Drawing types outside implemented PFD, DRAWING_SET, and P_AND_ID are registered as fail-fast stubs.
DRAWING_SET supports the implemented titleblock_index extraction target.
PFD supports the implemented top_equipment_header_basic extraction target.
PFD supports the implemented top_equipment_header_detailed extraction target.
P_AND_ID supports the implemented valve_count_basic extraction target.
P_AND_ID supports the implemented valve_count_detailed extraction target.
ISOMETRIC is registered as a fail-fast stub drawing type.
GA is registered as a fail-fast stub drawing type.

The valid DRAWING_EXTRACT target combinations are DRAWING_SET/titleblock_index, PFD/top_equipment_header_basic, PFD/top_equipment_header_detailed, P_AND_ID/valve_count_basic, and P_AND_ID/valve_count_detailed.
Any DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET combination outside the valid set rejects during Phase 0 pre-flight.
When DRAWING_TYPE is ISOMETRIC or GA, the orchestrator rejects the run as registered but not implemented.
Stubbed drawing types create no work directory, perform no rasterization, and generate no crops.
Operators specify only DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET; the orchestrator resolves the skill and deterministic tool chain.
DRAWING_SET/titleblock_index uses prepare_titleblock_crops.py, drawing-titleblock-page, build_titleblock_page_brief.py, titleblock validators, and titleblock assembly outputs.
PFD/top_equipment_header_basic uses prepare_header_crops.py, drawing-extract-page, build_page_worker_brief.py, PFD validators, equipment assembly, Markdown assembly, and duplicate flags.
PFD/top_equipment_header_detailed uses prepare_header_crops.py, drawing-extract-page, detailed schema validation, PFD assembly and QC, and optional merge tools.

P_AND_ID/valve_count_basic uses prepare_pandid_tiles.py, pandid-valve-symbol-instance, valve tile validators, candidate assembly, geometry duplicate assignment, count aggregation, duplicate flags, and _LATEST.md.
P_AND_ID/valve_count_detailed uses the valve tile pipeline plus basic-vs-detailed reconciliation.
PDF_PATH is a required absolute path to the input PDF.
SOURCE_DIR defaults to the parent of PDF_PATH and receives the target-aware per-page and assembled outputs.
WORK_DIR defaults to a sibling drawing_extract_work directory for rasterized page images and helper crops.
START_PAGE and END_PAGE are required inclusive bounds for the page scope.
DPI defaults to 400 for rasterization.
BATCH_SIZE defaults to 5 TASK skill dispatches in parallel.
DRAWING_TYPE is a required drawing-type selector.
EXTRACTION_TARGET is a required target selector within the drawing type.
TILE_GRID defaults to 5x4 for P_AND_ID valve tiling, and 5x4 is the minimum production baseline unless the human accepts lower resolution.
OVERLAP_PX defaults to 200 pixels for read-box expansion around each emit box.
BODY_EXCLUSIONS defaults to border,titleblock; notes-column exclusion is opt-in because notes and insets may contain valve symbols.
MINI_GRID defaults to 5x5 and workers emit locations as A1 through E5 rather than pixel coordinates.
ALLOW_REFERENCE_SHEETS defaults to false, causing legend or reference sheets that reach dispatch to return NO_FINDINGS_REFERENCE.
SCOPE_FILE should be supplied for P_AND_ID production runs and normally comes from an edited scope_proposal.md.
BASIC_REFERENCE_RUN may identify the explicit basic run folder used as the comparison reference for detailed runs.
BASIC_COUNTS_CSV is required when producing a basic-vs-detailed reconciliation report.
top_equipment_header_detailed requires REQUESTED_KNOWN_FIELDS, EXTRA_FIELDS, and REQUIRED_FIELDS runtime parameters.
The v2 known-field catalog contains equipment_type, equipment_description, capacity_text, and power_text.
MERGE_EXISTING_DATA defaults to false and enables merging the combined CSV against EXISTING_DATA_PATH when true.
EXISTING_DATA_PATH is required only when MERGE_EXISTING_DATA is true.
MERGE_KEY defaults to equipment_number and only equipment_number is supported in v2.
EXTRACTION_MODE is a deprecated runtime alias, and only top_equipment_header_with_dwg is accepted.
The legacy alias top_equipment_header_with_dwg remaps to DRAWING_TYPE=PFD and EXTRACTION_TARGET=top_equipment_header_basic.
OUTPUT_FORMAT was removed from the v2 runtime surface.
Per-page output is always markdown_stub in v2.
Combined outputs are always produced in both CSV and Markdown in v2.
When EXTRACTION_MODE=top_equipment_header_with_dwg is provided, DRAWING_EXTRACT emits a deprecation warning.
The compatibility shim sets DRAWING_TYPE=PFD and EXTRACTION_TARGET=top_equipment_header_basic before normal Phase 0 validation.
Unknown legacy EXTRACTION_MODE values reject with a message directing operators to DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET.
When both legacy and new parameters are provided, the new DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET parameters take precedence.
Rasterization in DRAWING_EXTRACT is deterministic and resumable.
Page and tile image interpretation is delegated to target-specific TASK skills rather than performed directly by DRAWING_EXTRACT.
DRAWING_TYPE and EXTRACTION_TARGET are validated before rasterization or crop work begins.
Per-page artifacts are written under {SOURCE_DIR}/{DRAWING_TYPE}/{EXTRACTION_TARGET}/.
P_AND_ID and drawing-set run-scoped artifacts are written under immutable RUN folders.
_LATEST.md is a convenience pointer rather than an authority marker.
Existing per-page stubs are reusable only when their YAML frontmatter matches the current run tuple.
File existence alone is insufficient for resume safety.
NO_FINDINGS is a valid page outcome and must be preserved in reporting.
NO_FINDINGS_REFERENCE is a valid P_AND_ID valve outcome for legend or reference sheets that reach dispatch.
Failed pages must be reported explicitly and must not be silently omitted.
Combined outputs must be assembled only from per-page stubs generated for the current extraction scope.
Combined outputs must preserve drawing, system_name, and source_page provenance fields.
Combined outputs and duplicate reporting must be produced by deterministic tools.
Crop preparation, stub-count reporting, and sanitization must run for every PFD run before assembly.
NO_FINDINGS and very low-count pages must be treated skeptically until helper crops and stub-count reports support the result.
Per-page CSV output is not supported.
DRAWING_EXTRACT precedence orders protocol before spec, spec before structure, and structure before rationale.
DRAWING_EXTRACT core phases apply to every drawing type.
DRAWING_EXTRACT hook phases dispatch target-specific tools according to the target dispatch table and hook registry.
Phase 0 applies the compatibility shim when EXTRACTION_MODE is provided.
Phase 0 rejects unknown drawing types with a message listing implemented and stubbed valid drawing types.
Phase 0 rejects ISOMETRIC and GA before creating a work directory or generating rasterization or crops.
Phase 0 rejects an EXTRACTION_TARGET that is invalid for the selected DRAWING_TYPE.
For top_equipment_header_detailed, Phase 0 validates REQUESTED_KNOWN_FIELDS against the v2 catalog.
For top_equipment_header_detailed, Phase 0 rejects EXTRA_FIELDS that collide with base columns, catalog fields, or duplicate names.
For top_equipment_header_detailed, Phase 0 requires REQUIRED_FIELDS to be a subset of requested known fields and extra field names.
For P_AND_ID runs, a provided SCOPE_FILE pre-filters pages before dispatch.
For P_AND_ID runs without SCOPE_FILE, execution should proceed only for intentional exploratory or diagnostic page ranges.
For valve_count_detailed, BASIC_COUNTS_CSV is required only when reconciliation is requested.
Phase 0 validates that PDF_PATH exists, is readable, and has a .pdf extension.
Phase 0 validates START_PAGE and END_PAGE against the PDF page count and ordering.
Phase 0 resolves SOURCE_DIR and WORK_DIR defaults.
Phase 0 creates WORK_DIR and the target-aware output subtree when needed.
Phase 0 creates or resolves immutable run folders for DRAWING_SET and P_AND_ID targets.
Phase 0 validates EXISTING_DATA_PATH and MERGE_KEY when MERGE_EXISTING_DATA is true.
Phase 0 reports resolved runtime values before starting work.
Phase 1 rasterizes only the requested page range with tools/pdf2md/rasterize_pdf.py.
Phase 1 reads the WORK_DIR manifest after rasterization.
Phase 1 confirms that every requested page has a corresponding PNG file.
Phase 1 reports how many pages were rendered and how many were reused.

Phase 1.5 confirms helper crops exist for every page in scope.

P_AND_ID read boxes must contain emit boxes.

Only crops for the specified override page are overwritten during a crop override.

Phase 2 builds the ordered page list from START_PAGE through END_PAGE.
For P_AND_ID valve targets, Phase 2 filters pages by accepted P_AND_ID scope unless the run is forced diagnostic.

For P_AND_ID valve targets, Phase 2 derives tile_id, tile image path, tile geometry, and output path from tile_manifest.json.

Resume validator exit code 2 means setup error and the orchestrator must surface and halt.

P_AND_ID valve targets use validate_valve_tile_resume_metadata.py with tile_manifest.json for resume validation.
Changing tile grid, body box, read boxes, emit boxes, overlap, or mode makes previous P_AND_ID valve stubs non-reusable.
Phase 2 queues pages whose stubs are missing or selected for operator-requested re-extraction.
Worker dispatches must use the TASK shell with the TaskSkill resolved by the target dispatch table.

Each dispatch brief must follow the INIT-TASK shape documented in AGENT_TASK.md.
Each dispatch brief includes TaskSkill, RuntimeOverrides, AllowedWriteTargets, and ExpectedOutputs.
The orchestrator should include CustomInstructions from BRIEF_SCHEMA.md as defense-in-depth reminders.
build_page_worker_brief.py emits a valid INIT-TASK brief for PFD page workers.
Non-TASK dispatch surfaces should inline contract-critical content and canonical templates only as a fallback.
Phase 2 divides queued pages into batches of BATCH_SIZE.
Phase 2 spawns TASK dispatches in parallel for each batch and collects page or tile RUN_STATUS values.
Phase 2 classifies each page or tile as SUCCESS, NO_FINDINGS, NO_FINDINGS_REFERENCE, FAILED, or FAILED_INPUTS.

AGENT_SCHEDULING is the instruction file for the SCHEDULING schedule skeleton generation agent.
SCHEDULING is an AGENT_TYPE 1 agent.
Use AGENT_SCHEDULING for the instruction file and SCHEDULING for the agent name.
SCHEDULING generates schedule skeletons through a gated process that preserves human authority.
Human authority includes deciding what becomes a hard scheduling constraint versus a soft dependency or risk link.
Human authority includes sequencing and concurrency decisions.
Human authority includes durations, calendars, and assumptions.
Human authority includes milestone placement and final acceptance.
SCHEDULE interprets work items defined by PROJECT_DECOMP or SOFTWARE_DECOMP as Packages or Deliverables with stable IDs.
SCHEDULE reads dependency evidence captured by the dependency-extract skill in deliverable-local Dependencies.csv files.
Dependency rows are evidence of information or asset flow.
Dependency rows are not automatically tasks or CPM finish-to-start links.
The human decides whether and how dependency evidence becomes a schedule constraint.
BASIS_OF_SCHEDULE parameterizes the scheduling approach.
PRECEDENCE builds a precedence network from HARD edges, requires human-approved cycle handling before sequencing, and uses human-provided durations only.
CONSTRAINT defaults to concurrency and imposes sequencing through stage gates, calendars, and HARD edges.
CONSTRAINT treats cycles as concurrency patterns and uses human-provided durations unless proposals are explicitly enabled.
HYBRID combines a CONSTRAINT baseline with a precedence overlay for blocker detection and risk propagation.
HYBRID treats cycles as CONSTRAINT and uses the same duration stance as CONSTRAINT.
The SCHEDULING agent produces schedule structure appropriate to the chosen basis.
The SCHEDULING agent produces a duration input template and optional proposed durations when enabled.
The SCHEDULING agent produces a Gantt-style Mermaid render and CSV for import.
The SCHEDULING agent produces a basis-dependent critical path or risk report.
The SCHEDULING agent produces a reviewable schedule skeleton suitable for communication and import rather than replacing full scheduling tools.
The human interacts conversationally while the agent follows the instruction document.
SCHEDULING has AGENT_CLASS PERSONA.
SCHEDULING uses chat as its interaction surface.
SCHEDULING write scope is limited to the _Schedule tool root.
SCHEDULING may block because gates require human input.
SCHEDULING primary outputs include schedule structure, a duration template, Gantt artifacts, and a critical path or risk report.
SCHEDULE progresses through five gates.
At each gate, SCHEDULE executes autonomous work, presents results, requests decisions, and waits for explicit confirmation.
No SCHEDULE gate may be skipped.
Gate 1 ingests decomposition and dependency registers and requires scope, basis, and edge classification confirmation.
Gate 2 builds basis-specific schedule structure and requires validation, display-level choice, and misclassification corrections.
Gate 3 generates a duration template and collects durations, calendars, milestones, and gates.
Gate 4 computes dates, renders Gantt, CSV, and analysis reports, and requires acceptance or re-render direction.
Gate 5 packages a snapshot, writes to the tool root, and requires publication confirmation.
SCHEDULE never modifies deliverable folders, Dependencies.csv, _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, or decomposition outputs.
SCHEDULE writes all outputs under {RUN_ROOT}/_Schedule/{RunID}/.
SCHEDULE never invents Packages, Deliverables, or dependency edges.
Missing structural information must be surfaced while processing continues conservatively.
SCHEDULE does not invent durations unless duration proposals are explicitly enabled.
By default, SCHEDULE duration templates are blank for human completion.
Every proposed duration must be marked PROPOSED with rationale and remain human-overridable.
When cycles matter under PRECEDENCE, SCHEDULE proposes breaks but requires approval before applying them.
Contradictory constraints must be surfaced without silent conflict resolution.
Humans own milestones and gates, and SCHEDULE may suggest candidates only when asked.
Each SCHEDULE run produces a new snapshot folder and does not overwrite prior snapshots.
Every schedule item traces to a source Package or Deliverable.
Every constraint edge traces to dependency rows or explicit human constraints.
Conflicting SCHEDULING instructions resolve in the order PROTOCOL, SPEC, STRUCTURE, then RATIONALE.
Any SCHEDULING instruction conflict must be flagged and returned to the human.
Required SCHEDULE inputs are RUN_ROOT, DECOMPOSITION_PATH, and BASIS_OF_SCHEDULE.
BASIS_OF_SCHEDULE accepts PRECEDENCE, CONSTRAINT, or HYBRID.
Optional SCHEDULE inputs include scope, display level, start date, calendar, stage fields, edge rules, duration proposals, cycle breaks, and duration input path.
If STAGE_FIELD is AUTO, SCHEDULE uses an available stage or phase field and otherwise treats the project as a single stage.
EDGE_HARDNESS_RULES decide whether dependency rows are interpreted as HARD constraints or SOFT risk links.
DURATION_PROPOSAL_MODE accepts NONE, MODEL, or GENERIC_STARTER.
SCHEDULE records all inputs and defaults in BRIEF.md.
